Reversing polarity inverts both stimulus artifact and the cochlear microphonic.
So polarity alone cannot tell them apart.
To be sure, record a control run with the sound tube clamped.
An oscillation that disappears is a true cochlear microphonic.
One that stays unchanged is electrical artifact.
